primitives.title: Intake, scope definition, and materiality thresholds
primitives.objective: Clarify the analysis period, reporting basis, segment/granularity, and define materiality rules to focus on meaningful P&L movements.
primitives.capability: Gather requirements (periods, actual vs budget/forecast, segment cuts, currency), define materiality (absolute, % of revenue/EBITDA, statistical), set deliverable format and audience expectations.
acceptance: Documented scope: periods (e.g., monthly last 24 months), comparison baselines (YoY, QoQ, vs budget), and consolidation level (company/segment/product/region).
Materiality thresholds agreed (e.g., >= $X and/or >= Y% of revenue/EBITDA) plus exception handling for strategically important items.
Data sources and owners confirmed (ERP, planning system, data warehouse) and a data dictionary outline drafted.

## P01 — Intake, scope definition, and materiality thresholds (per SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5)

### 1) Scope decisions to confirm (required)
Please confirm or fill the **[TBD]** fields. If you don’t have a preference, I included **recommended defaults**.

**A. Analysis period & cadence**
- Period cadence: **Monthly** (recommended)
- Coverage window: **Last 24 months** ending **[TBD month/year]** (recommended)
- Include partial/current month? **[TBD: Yes/No]** (default: No; use closed months only)

**B. Comparison baselines**
Select which to include (recommended: all three if available):
- **YoY**: current month vs same month prior year (Yes/No) → **[TBD]**
- **MoM**: current month vs prior month (Yes/No) → **[TBD]**
- **YTD vs prior year YTD** (Yes/No) → **[TBD]**
- **Actuals vs Budget** (Yes/No) → **[TBD]**
- **Actuals vs Forecast / Latest Estimate (LE)** (Yes/No) → **[TBD]**

**C. Reporting basis (accounting & definitions)**
- Basis: **[TBD: GAAP / IFRS / Local / Management]**
- Revenue recognition policy impacts to note: **[TBD]**
- EBITDA definition: **[TBD: Mgmt Adj EBITDA vs Reported Operating Income]**
- Treatment of one-time items: **[TBD: included in EBITDA? excluded?]**
- FX presentation: **[TBD: reported FX / constant currency]** (recommend both if global)

**D. Consolidation level & granularity**
- Consolidation: **Company-wide consolidated** (default) + drill-downs
- Drill-down dimensions (choose what exists in your data):
  - Segment / Business unit: **[TBD]**
  - Product / SKU family: **[TBD]**
  - Region / country: **[TBD]**
  - Channel / customer type: **[TBD]**
  - Customer top-N: **[TBD]**
- Minimum required P&L line depth (recommended):
  - Revenue (and volume/price/mix if available)
  - COGS (materials, labor, freight, etc. if available)
  - Gross profit
  - Opex: Sales & Marketing, R&D, G&A (and key subaccounts)
  - EBITDA / Operating income
  - Below-the-line: D&A, interest, taxes (optional per request) **[TBD]**

**E. Output audience & constraints**
- Audience: **Exec/ELT/Board** (assumed from request)
- Presentation currency: **[TBD currency]**
- Rounding: **[TBD: $000 / $M]** (default: $000 for internal, $M for board)
- Confidentiality constraints / restricted items: **[TBD]**

---

### 2) Materiality thresholds (proposal for agreement)
To focus on “meaningful movements,” I propose **dual triggers** (absolute + relative) plus **strategic exceptions**.

**A. Primary materiality rule (recommended)**
Flag a driver/variance if it meets **either**:
1) **Absolute impact ≥ max($250k, 0.5% of TTM revenue)**, **or**
2) **EBITDA impact ≥ 1.0% of TTM EBITDA** (use if EBITDA is a key focus)

**B. Secondary rule by line type (recommended)**
- Revenue variances: flag if **≥ 1.0% of revenue** or **≥ $500k**
- Gross margin rate: flag if **≥ 50 bps** change **and** **≥ $250k** GP impact
- Opex lines: flag if **≥ $200k** or **≥ 3% of that cost line**

**C. Exception handling (explicit)**
Always surface items even if below thresholds when:
- New product/region launch, major customer win/loss, pricing program
- Restructuring, litigation, regulatory events
- Material accounting policy changes / reclasses
- FX-driven swings in priority markets
- Exec-designated “watchlist” accounts (you provide list)

**D. Aggregation logic**
- Avoid “peanut-buttering”: small accounts can be grouped into “Other” unless:
  - multiple small accounts share a common root cause (then roll up as one driver)
- Track reclasses explicitly to prevent false variances (needs mapping support)

**Items to confirm**
- Do you prefer thresholds tied to **Revenue**, **EBITDA**, or **Operating Income**?
- Preferred absolute threshold: **$100k / $250k / $500k / $1M**?

---

Please identify the system-of-record for each. If multiple exist, specify the “gold” source.

**A. Actuals (GL / ERP)**
- System: **[TBD: NetSuite / SAP / Oracle / Dynamics / other]**
- Data owner (Finance/Accounting): **[TBD name/team]**
- Close calendar: **[TBD]**
- Entities included/excluded: **[TBD]**

**B. Budget / Forecast**
- System: **[TBD: Anaplan / Adaptive / Hyperion / Excel / other]**
- Owner (FP&A): **[TBD]**
- Versioning: Budget FY**[TBD]**, Forecast version **[TBD]**, last refresh **[TBD]**

**C. Dimensional master data**
- Chart of Accounts owner: **[TBD]**
- Cost centers / departments: **[TBD]**
- Product hierarchy: **[TBD]**
- Customer hierarchy / CRM link: **[TBD: Salesforce etc.]**
- FX rates source: **[TBD: Treasury, Oanda, ERP rates]**

**D. Data delivery format**
- Preferred: **CSV/Excel extracts** or **warehouse tables** (Snowflake/BigQuery/etc.) **[TBD]**
- Timing: **[TBD date]**
- Access constraints: **[TBD]**

---

### 4) Data dictionary outline (draft)
This is the minimum dictionary needed to run the trend + driver attribution cleanly.

**Core fact table: P&L Actuals (monthly)**
- Period (YYYY-MM)
- Entity / legal entity
- Consolidation scope flag
- Currency (local + reporting)
- Account code + account name
- P&L line mapping (Revenue/COGS/Opex etc.)
- Cost center / department
- Product (if applicable)
- Customer / channel (if applicable)
- Region / country
- Amount (signed convention defined)
- Source system + extract timestamp

**Plan table: Budget/Forecast (monthly)**

- Version (Budget/Forecast1/LE)
- Amount

**Reference tables**
- COA to P&L mapping (including reclass history)
- Org hierarchy (cost center rollups)
- Product hierarchy
- Customer hierarchy
- FX rates (avg vs end-of-period, by currency)

**Open definition questions**
- Sign convention: revenue positive or negative? **[TBD]**
- Do we have quantities for volume/price/mix decomposition? **[TBD]**

---

### 5) Evidence, assumptions, unresolved gaps (as required)

**Evidence (from user request)**
- You requested: “Analyze a company’s P&L trend, identify material drivers, and prepare an executive-ready findings package.”
- No periods, basis, segments, thresholds, or systems were provided.

**Assumptions (pending your confirmation)**

**Unresolved gaps / required inputs**

2) Reporting basis (GAAP/IFRS/management) and EBITDA definition
3) Baselines to include (YoY/MoM/YTD vs PY/vs Budget/vs Forecast)
4) Consolidation scope and required drill-down dimensions
5) Materiality thresholds preferences

## P03 — P&L trend baseline and variance decomposition (SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5)

### Evidence (inputs received)
- No P&L dataset, trial balance extract, budget/forecast, or benchmark file was provided in the request.
- Therefore, no numeric trend, exhibits, or reconciled variance bridges can yet be computed.

### Assumptions (pending confirmation)
- “Agreed periods” = at minimum **Current period vs Prior Year** and **Actual vs Budget** (e.g., FY2025 vs FY2024; FY2025A vs FY2025B), plus interim (monthly/quarterly) if available.
- Standard P&L structure available: **Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Opex (by function), EBITDA/EBIT**, plus margins.
- Benchmarks (if any) are either internal plan/forecast or external comps; format TBD.

### Unresolved gaps (must be provided to execute P03)
Please provide (or confirm) the following:
1. **P&L actuals** by period (monthly/quarterly preferred) for at least two comparable periods.
2. **Budget/forecast** by the same line items and periods (if “vs benchmarks” includes budget).
3. **Chart of accounts mapping** to functions for Opex (e.g., S&M, R&D, G&A, Ops).
4. **Revenue/COGS drivers** to enable price/volume/mix (any of):
   - Units/volume, average selling price (ASP), product/customer/region mix, discounting
   - For COGS: units, standard cost, freight, labor rates, materials index, yield/scrap
5. **Any non-recurring items** to normalize (restructuring, legal settlements, one-time credits).
6. **Definition choices**: EBITDA vs EBIT treatment (D&A, stock comp, rent add-backs, etc.).

---

## Deliverable package (what I will produce once data is provided)

### A) Standardized trend exhibits (per Acceptance)
1. **Revenue trend** (by period): $ and % growth  
2. **COGS trend**: $ and % of revenue  
3. **Gross Profit & GM%**: $ and margin trend  
4. **Opex by function**: $ and % of revenue (S&M, R&D, G&A, Other)  
5. **EBITDA and/or EBIT**: $ and margin trend  
6. **Optional**: Operating income, net income if available/needed

**Output format:** executive-ready tables + charts (waterfalls and sparklines), with consistent sign conventions and footnotes.

### B) Variance decomposition & bridges (reconciling baseline → current)
For each key line item (Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Opex, EBITDA/EBIT):
- **Bridge 1:** Prior Year → Current Year (YoY)
- **Bridge 2:** Budget → Actual (BvA)

**Bridge logic (example structure):**
- Revenue Δ = Volume + Price/Rate + Mix + FX (if applicable) + Other/One-time
- COGS Δ = Volume + Unit cost (rate) + Mix + Freight/inputs + Other
- Opex Δ = Headcount/Comp + Variable spend + Program timing + One-time

Each bridge will **reconcile exactly** from baseline to current (tie-out check shown).

### C) Price/Volume/Mix decomposition (where data allows)
If revenue is available by product/customer/region with units and price:
- **Volume effect:** (Units_current − Units_base) × Price_base  
- **Price effect:** (Price_current − Price_base) × Units_base  
- **Mix effect:** residual after price & volume (or via weighted mix method)  
**Assumption disclosure:** base period weights, treatment of new/discontinued SKUs, FX handling.

If only dollars are available (no units):
- Decomposition will be **proxy-based** (e.g., by segment growth and implied ASP), clearly labeled as such.

---

## Data template (minimum fields to send)
A single Excel/CSV is fine.

**P&L table:**
- Period (YYYY-MM or YYYY-Q)
- Revenue
- COGS
- S&M Opex
- R&D Opex
- G&A Opex
- Other Opex (optional)
- D&A (if EBIT required)
- Stock comp / one-time items (optional, but helpful)
- Actual / Budget flag (or separate columns)

**Driver table (optional but preferred):**
- Period
- Segment/Product/Region/Customer
- Units
- Revenue
- (Optional) COGS, units cost, freight, etc.

---

## Next step (to proceed)
Upload the P&L actuals (and budget/benchmark if applicable) and confirm:
1) periods to analyze, 2) EBITDA vs EBIT definition, 3) any normalization items.

Once received, I will return the **P03 package**: standardized trend exhibits + reconciled variance bridges + price/volume/mix (where supported), with evidence notes and any remaining gaps.

## P04 — Material driver identification & ranking (SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5)

### Evidence available
- No P&L dataset, variance bridge, or segment/time breakdown was provided in the prompt.
- Therefore I cannot quantify impacts, rank drivers, or validate tie-out to the analysis dataset yet.

### Assumptions (to proceed once data is provided)
- We are explaining **Period B vs Period A** (e.g., Actual vs Prior Year, or Actual vs Budget) for each P&L line.
- “Material drivers” will be ranked to explain **~80% of total variance per line** (configurable to 70–90%).
- Drivers can be decomposed into standard levers: **Volume, Price, Mix, FX, One-time items, Cost inflation, Productivity, Headcount, Rate, Utilization**, etc., depending on line.

### Unresolved gaps / required inputs (minimum)
Provide one of the following:
1) **Transaction/GL-level dataset** with fields: `period`, `P&L line`, `amount`, plus available dimensions (e.g., `product`, `customer`, `region`, `channel`, `cost center`, `vendor`, `headcount`, `units`, `price`, `FX rate`), **or**
2) **Pre-aggregated variance cube** by `P&L line × period × segment` with Period A/B amounts.

Also specify:
- Comparison: **(A vs B)** and date range
- Materiality threshold (optional): e.g., “rank until 80% explained or top 10, whichever first”
- Segments that matter (if any): region/product/channel/etc.

---

## Output (template) — Ranked driver list per P&L line
Once data is available, I will deliver tables like below for **each major P&L line** (Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, OpEx sub-lines, EBITDA, etc.).

### Example structure (to be populated with your data)

#### Revenue — variance explained target: 80%
| Rank | Driver | Quantified impact (Δ$) | Share of Revenue variance | Periods impacted | Segments impacted | Structural vs temporary | Evidence / tie-out |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Price change | +X | Y% | 2026-Q2 | NA / Product A | Structural | Bridge: Price lever; ties to avg selling price |
| 2 | Volume decline | -X | Y% | 2026-Q2 | EMEA / Channel B | Temporary | Units shipped |
| 3 | Mix shift | +X | Y% | Apr–Jun | SKU mix | Structural | Mix variance calc |
| 4 | FX | -X | Y% | May–Jun | Intl | Temporary | FX rate vs constant currency |
| 5 | One-time recognition | +X | Y% | June | Customer Z | Temporary | JE / contract milestone |

**Cumulative explained:** XX% (stop when target met or top N reached)

#### COGS — variance explained target: 80%
| Rank | Driver | Quantified impact (Δ$) | Share of COGS variance | Periods impacted | Segments impacted | Structural vs temporary | Evidence / tie-out |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Input cost inflation | +X | Y% | Q2 | Materials | Structural | Vendor pricing / PPV |
| 2 | Labor rate / OT | +X | Y% | May | Plant 2 | Temporary | Timekeeping |
| 3 | Volume-related absorption | +X | Y% | Q2 | Plant network | Temporary | Utilization/absorption calc |
| 4 | Freight | +X | Y% | Apr–Jun | E-commerce | Temporary | Freight per shipment |
| 5 | Inventory write-down | +X | Y% | June | SKU set | Temporary | Non-recurring charge |

…and similarly for SG&A, R&D, Marketing, Other Income/Expense, etc.

---

## Method (what I will run once data is provided)
1) **Compute variances** for each P&L line: Δ = Period B – Period A.
2) **Decompose** each line into candidate drivers using available dimensions:
   - Revenue: price/volume/mix/FX/customer concentration
   - COGS: volume/absorption, input prices, labor, yield/scrap, freight, duties, FX
   - OpEx: headcount, comp rate, bonus accruals, program spend, timing, one-offs
3) **Rank drivers by absolute Δ$ impact**, then compute cumulative % of total variance explained.
4) **Select top drivers** until reaching the defined explained-share threshold (70–90%) or top N.
5) **Classify structural vs temporary** using flags:
   - structural: recurring run-rate changes (pricing policy, org changes, sustained rate changes)
   - temporary: timing shifts, true one-time charges/credits, short-lived spikes
6) **Tie-out checks**:
   - Driver impacts sum to total variance (within rounding)
   - Reconcile to variance bridge totals and source dataset aggregates

---

## What I need from you to produce the actual ranked drivers
Upload or paste:
- P&L by month/quarter for Period A and Period B (with segments if available), and
- Any operational metrics you have (units, headcount, FX, price) if you want true driver decomposition (not just segment contribution).

If you share the dataset, I will return the **ranked top 5–10 drivers per P&L line** with **quantified Δ$**, **period/segment attribution**, and **structural vs temporary**, explaining **~80% (or your chosen threshold)** of each line’s movement.

- Reconciliation plan if disagreement: __________________

**Implications (run-rate, risk/opportunity, persistence):**
- Expected persistence: **(structural/temporary/one-time)** because __________
- Run-rate: **+$__/quarter** if sustained; sensitivity: **1% price = $__**
- Risks: reversal in renewals, competitive response, regulatory constraints
- Actions: maintain guardrails, target segments, tighten discounting

---

### Driver 2: __________________ (Impact: $___)
**Facts:** …
**Hypothesis:** …
**Evidence:** …
**Validation:** …
**Implications:** …

### Driver 3: __________________ (Impact: $___)
…

*(Typically 5–8 drivers covering ~80–90% of variance.)*

---

## 3) Clear Separation: Facts vs Assumptions vs Open Questions

### Facts (grounded items only)
- F1: __________________
- F2: __________________

### Assumptions (explicit, to be validated)
- A1: __________________ (why assumed; what would falsify it)
- A2: __________________

### Open questions / gaps (what’s missing, who owns, due date)
- Q1: __________________ | Owner: __ | Due: __ | Needed data: __
- Q2: __________________ | Owner: __ | Due: __

---

## 4) Validation Loop (SOP-style control)
**Objective:** Convert hypotheses into validated root causes with audit trail.

### Stepwise loop (per driver)
1. **Restate variance** and tie to the bridge number (single source of truth).
2. **Propose 1–3 hypotheses** maximum per driver (mutually exclusive where possible).
3. **Pull corroborating KPIs** (leading + lagging) and any policy/accounting notes.
4. **Stakeholder check** (Finance BP + functional owner):
   - Questions to ask:
     - “What operational change explains this variance?”
     - “Is this timing, mix, pricing, or accounting?”
     - “What would you expect next month/quarter?”
5. **Document outcome**: confirmed / partially confirmed / rejected; log evidence links.
6. **Implication tagging**: run-rate, persistence, controllability, risk level.

### Validation tracker (table)
| Driver | Hypothesis | Evidence links/KPIs | Stakeholders | Status | Next step | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

---

## 5) Executive “Implications” Summary (one slide worth)
- **Sustaining tailwinds:** (Driver __, __) → estimated run-rate **+$__**
- **Transient headwinds:** (Driver __) → likely to unwind by __
- **Structural issues to address:** (Driver __) → requires action in __
- **Accounting/policy items:** (Driver __) → disclosure / normalization needed

---

## What I need from you to complete this
Paste either:
- The **variance bridge** (Revenue, GM, Opex, etc.) with top drivers and amounts; or
- The P&L by month with a note of what you consider “material,” and I’ll map it into drivers if the quantified list isn’t ready.

Also tell me:
- Audience (CEO/CFO/Board), and whether you want **1-page memo**, **3-slide narrative**, or **talk track**.
